verdicts.flaw_description: A named alternative cause covers all four runs: "Every shop refitted its machines with a faster insert grade that quarter, and every logged run was cut on one of those machines." A faster insert grade directly shortens cycle time, so the 4-7 minute reductions cannot be attributed to the coolant.

In two of the four cases the outcome is measured before the kit was issued: case one was issued 4 November but completion was read "by 27 September", and case three was issued 5 June but read "by 28 April". The effect precedes the cause in half the evidence.

A named alternative cause covers all four lines: "Premium stock's share of each store's shelf hit a record, double the earlier period, and every line was stocked straight from that shelf." Doubling premium mix raises revenue per order on its own, so the 4-7 percent lift is not attributable to the pricing rule.

The measured quantity is not the one the claim is about: the claim is that the timetable "reduces absence", but every case reports only that "lateness ran 6/4/7/5 percent below the same cohort a term earlier". Pupils arriving late are present, so lateness figures say nothing about absence.
